title: Tattva x felt-essence (research-only)

voice.text: "The essential nature of light is reflective awareness (vimarśa); otherwise light, though
'coloured' by objects, would be similar to an insentient reality, such as crystal and so
on."
Vṛtti: "Reflective awareness (pratyavamarśa) constitutes the primary essence (mukhya
ātman) of light. In the absence of this reflective awareness, light, though objects make
it assume different forms, would merely be 'limpid', but not sentient, since there is no
'savouring' (camatkṛteḥ)."
"prakāśasya mukhya ātmā pratyavamarśaḥ… Sans elle, cette manifestation… n'aurait que la
limpidité [d'un miroir], mais pas la spontanéité (ajaḍya), parce qu'elle ne comporterait
pas d'émerveillement (camatkṛti)."
"Apperception is the fundamental essence of conscious manifestation. Without it, this
manifestation, even having the differentiated aspect of this or that object, would have
only the limpidity [of a mirror], but not spontaneity, because it would not involve
wonder (camatkṛti)."
"The fundamental form of consciousness is not something cognitive, like vision; rather,
it is something affective… the primary function of consciousness is not perceiving or
remembering or comprehending but feeling."
"if the cortex is absent, consciousness ought to disappear. In the case of hydranencephalic
children this appears not to happen… They are not comatose and nor do they exist in a
vegetative state." (1722–1730)
"I think there is 'something it is like' to be a hydranencephalic child." (2157–2159)

claims.text: yad idaṃ vibhavātmakaṃ bhuvanajātam uktaṃ garbhīkṛtānantavicitrabhoktṛbhogyaṃ — this world-born glory-natured, wombing endless varied enjoyer-enjoyed.
tatra yad anugataṃ mahāprakāśarūpaṃ — what pervades as great-light-formed.
tat mahāsāmānyakalpaṃ paramaśivarūpam — that is like the great common, Supreme-Śiva-formed.
Paramaśiva = what pervades the whole as great light.
yat tu katipayakatipayabhedānugataṃ rūpaṃ tat tattvam — what pervades only some differences: a category.
yathā pṛthivī nāma ... samastabrahmāṇḍānugatā — as earth, pervading all world-eggs from Kālāgni to Vīrabhadra.
Partial pervasion defines tattva; earth the example.
